333: Auction of 2 Year Notes
334: 
335: On October 14 the Treasury announced that it would auction $4,500 million of 2 year notes to refund $1,130 million of notes maturing October 11, 1980, and to raise $1,110 million new cash. The notes offered were Treasury Notes of Series X-1982, to be dated October 11, 1980, due October 11, 1982, with interest payable on April 10 and October 11 in each year until maturity. A coupon rate of 12-1/4% was set after the determination as to which tenders were accepted on a yield basis, the average of which translated into an average accepted price close to 100.000.
336: 
337: Tenders for the notes were received until 1:10 p.m., EDT, October 22 and totaled $8,500 million, of which $6,500 million was accepted at yields ranging from 12.19%, price 99.888 up to 12.26%, price 99.767. Noncompetitive tenders for $1 million or less from any one bidder were accepted in full at the average yield of accepted tenders, 12.24%, price 99.801. These totaled $1,346 million. The $4,500 million of accepted tenders also included $583 million of tenders at the average price from Federal Reserve Banks as agents for foreign and international monetary authorities in exchange for securities maturing October 31, 1980.
338: 
339: In addition to the $4,500 million of tenders accepted in the auction process, $420 million of tenders were accepted at the average price from Government accounts and Federal Reserve Banks for their own account in exchange for maturing securities.
340: 
341: Tenders were received at Federal Reserve banks and branches and at the Bureau of the Public Debt, Washington, D.C., Beater notes, with interest coupons attached, and notes registered as to principal and interest were authorized to be issued in denominations of $5,000, $10,000, $100,000, and $1,000,000.
342: 
343: November Retunding
344:
